findings.F1: Fees, not the forecast, sink the book: summed over all bars the fees came to 9.26 against a gross position gain of -1.51, which is 0.000533 fee against -0.000087 gross per coin-day, leaving the book's mean daily return at -0.000621 while holding the coins made +0.001190.
findings.F2: The book opens and closes a position every evening (fees summed 4.06 on the 21:00 bar, 1.04 on the 22:00 bar and 4.09 on the 23:00 bar), and the position earns a mean of only +0.000249 per bar on the 21:00 bar and loses -0.000429 per bar on the 22:00 bar (about 7,600 to 7,900 active bars each), so the second hour gives back more than the first gains.
findings.F3: The late-evening rise is real but sits earlier and around the trade window, not inside it: the mean 1-hour return across all coins is +0.000545 (t 6.75) on the 20:00 bar and +0.000436 (t 5.66) on the 21:00 bar, but -0.000039 (t -0.49) on the 22:00 bar, among the highest-t hours of the day.
findings.F4: At 21:00 the 2-hour return rises with the 24-hour return instead of with the 24-hour fall: by 24-hour-return quintile it runs from +0.000060 (t 0.18) in the deepest-fall quintile to +0.001240 (t 4.12) in the strongest-rise quintile, and the 72-hour return sorts it the same way (top quintile +0.001200, t 4.09). The book was long in exactly the cases that do not rise.
findings.F5: The fall-side long of the tested idea flips sign by year: after a 24-hour fall the 21:00 2-hour return was +0.002198 (t 3.54) in 2018 but -0.001353, -0.001312 and -0.001747 (t -2.42, -2.25, -3.73) in 2020 to 2022, while after a 24-hour rise it was positive in 2020 to 2024 (t 2.26 to 3.35).
findings.F6: From the 20:00 bar the 2-hour return is positive in four of the five 24-hour-return quintiles, and largest after the deepest 24-hour falls (+0.002171, t 6.65), next after the strongest rises (+0.001323, t 4.81), and near zero in the fourth quintile (-0.000006). That is about four times the 21:00 deepest-fall quintile's +0.000060.

ideas.idea: Over the next 2 hours from the 20:00 UTC bar, a coin's return is positive, and the larger the size of its 24-hour move, the larger that late-evening rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long from 20:00 to 22:00 UTC, more after a large daily move in either direction, because that is when the evening rise is large enough to cover a daily round trip's fee.
ideas.name: early-evening rise after large moves

ideas.idea: Over the next 2 hours from the 21:00 UTC bar, a coin's return is positive, and the stronger its 24-hour rise, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the late-evening long only after a daily run-up, sized by its strength, and refuse it after a daily drop, where the rise is absent.
ideas.name: late-evening rise after daily gain
